title: A protein-language-model workflow discovers high-activity kynureninase enzymes for tumor models
summary: A workflow combining homology search, protein-language-model embeddings and regression prioritized kynureninases by predicted catalytic activity. Researchers experimentally tested four top-ranked candidates; the most active had nearly twice the turnover number of the prior best, and enzyme treatment was associated with a 3.4-fold reduction in tumor weight in a mouse comparison.
ai_technology: Protein language model embeddings coupled with regression in the SeekRank enzyme-prioritization workflow
organization: Seoul National University; and Galux Inc.

evidence.tested: Researchers experimentally tested four top-ranked candidates; the most active had nearly twice the turnover number of the prior best, and enzyme treatment was associated with a 3.4-fold reduction in tumor weight in a mouse comparison.
evidence.unknown: The evidence is a published paper abstract; it describes an enzyme/treatment experiment in a mouse tumor model, not clinical efficacy. The reported tumor-weight reduction is model-specific; no claim of human therapeutic benefit is made.
evidence.ai_role: The model represented homologous kynureninase sequences with protein-language-model embeddings and regressed kinetic activity to rank enzyme candidates. Four high-ranked candidates were tested in vitro and in vivo; the abstract reports one with nearly two-fold improved turnover number and reduced tumor weight in a mouse model.
